title: Signal decay produced orphaned-route surge — remediation & postmortem
creator: Anika Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-01 (~09:12 UTC) a sudden spike in 5xx errors and latency was observed for customers routed to eu-west-1. The control plane continued to route traffic to a set of hosts that had been partially drained; those hosts returned inconsistent errors and partial responses which triggered automated fallback to smaller model variants. The fallback surge saturated alternate tiers and caused broad latency and cost impact for affected tenants. This ticket documents the timeline, root causes, short-term remediation, and planned long-term fixes.
root_cause: The routing signal aggregator applies an exponential decay to recent drain/health signals to smooth noise. During a control-plane rolling restart and a transient message backlog, the drain signals originating from the regional decommission workflow were decayed below the routing threshold and treated as stale. The allocator then selected nodes still present in routing tables but functionally drained in the data plane (FS-level decommission in progress). This mismatch led to widespread misrouting to incompatible host variants and cascaded fallbacks.
timeline: 2026-03-01 09:05 UTC — Region maintenance started (planned) 2026-03-01 09:10 UTC — First SRE alerts: increased 503s and timeouts for eu-west-1 routes 2026-03-01 09:12 UTC — Auto-fallbacks triggered to 'variant-small' for ~12% of requests 2026-03-01 09:15 UTC — Traffic engineering noticed simultaneous increase in token cost and error rates 2026-03-01 09:22 UTC — Emergency routing rule applied to quarantine eu-west-1 at the edge 2026-03-01 09:28 UTC — Hotfix deployed: treat drain signals as sticky for 30 minutes and force immediate tombstone reconciliation 2026-03-01 09:40 UTC — Error rates and latency begun returning to baseline 2026-03-01 10:00 UTC — Post-incident monitoring and incident call; incident declared resolved 2026-03-02 — Initial RCA drafted; engineering action items prioritized
detection: Detected by SRE alerting on 5xx rate and P50/P95 token latency for eu-west-1. Additional signals: a spike in fallback rate (auto-policy), token cost per request, and an increase in model-variant swap logs. Control-plane telemetry showed decay metrics crossing the routing threshold for many nodes despite decommission events in the node lifecycle log.
mitigation: 1) Emergency edge rule: blocked new allocations to eu-west-1 and rerouted new sessions to nearest healthy region to stop bleed. 2) Hotfix: changed aggregator policy to disable exponential decay for drain signals and applied immediate tombstone reconciliation runbook (controller force-write tombstones). 3) Backpressure: rate-limited fallback paths to avoid immediate cascade into lower tiers. 4) Ops: increased observability retention of drain signals for 72 hours to support investigation.
long_term_fixes: 1) Signal durability: treat decommission/drain events as sticky with monotonically increasing sequence numbers so they cannot be decayed until explicitly cleared. 2) Tombstone reconciliation: add periodic cross-check between lifecycle store and routing tables; introduce idempotent tombstone writes. 3) Compatibility guardrails: require variant-compatibility metadata check before routing; refuse route if incompatible variant set detected. 4) Circuit-breakers: per-region capacity circuit-breaker to prevent fallback amplification. 5) Chaos testing: add targeted chaos tests for control-plane restarts + drain workflows. 6) Telemetry: new dashboard and alert for 'routing decision deviation' (control-plane vs data-plane state).

ENG-142530: Variant-compatibility pre-check in router (owner: Luis Ortega, estimate: 3, due: 2026-04-11)
ENG-142540: Per-region circuit-breaker prototype and tests (owner: Anika Patel, estimate: 5, due: 2026-04-18)
ENG-142550: Add chaos test that restarts control plane during drains (owner: SRE team, estimate: 2, due: 2026-04-01)
ENG-142560: Dashboard + alert for routing decision divergence (owner: Observability team, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-21)
notes: Key lesson: smoothing heuristics that are appropriate for transient health noise are dangerous for member-lifecycle signals (drain/decommission). These signals must be treated as higher-fidelity, monotonic events. The immediate hotfix prevented further customer impact but also revealed gaps in the reconciliation path when control-plane restarts are in flight.
